conflicts.name: Ecuador's war on narco gangs
conflicts.reason: yellow: high gang violence met with curfews and mass arrests, below war level
conflicts.status: Fourth curfew of 2026 in five provinces to Nov 10; 218 arrests on first night
conflicts.summary: Ecuador's government has treated drug gangs as armed enemies since 2024, as cocaine routes made the coast one of the region's most violent areas. On 1 November President Noboa imposed a midnight-to-5am curfew through 10 November in Guayas, Manabí, Los Ríos, El Oro and Esmeraldas, the fourth this year, per Xinhua. The interior ministry reported 218 arrests on the first night, many for curfew breaches. The decree itself counts 483 homicides nationwide from 17 September to 13 October, only 7% of them at night, while Noboa says crime fell 40% during the September curfew.

latest.text: Ecuador's interior ministry says 218 people were arrested on the first curfew night. 155 of the police arrests were for breaking the curfew, and 91 kg of drugs were seized.

us_impact.text: Ecuador is a major cocaine transit route and sends gang suspects to the US for trial, but the notes show no measurable effect on Americans this month. The main links are drug flows and migration.

conflicts.name: US-Cuba confrontation
conflicts.reason: yellow: sanctions and oil squeeze with past hints at military options, no armed clashes
conflicts.status: Talks stalled per CBS; sanctions tighten; Cuba says measures hurt civilians
conflicts.summary: After the January ouster of Maduro, Washington halted Venezuelan oil shipments to Cuba and threatened tariffs on countries that fill the gap, deepening island-wide blackouts (AFP). Tension peaked in May, when US media reported the administration was seeking to indict Raul Castro over the 1996 shootdown of civilian planes, Washington sanctioned Cuba's intelligence agency and ministers, and President Diaz-Canel warned a US attack would bring a bloodbath. Since then the pressure has been mainly economic: OFAC tightened banking and travel rules around 30 September, while Trump said on 26 September he expected a deal and did not think military force would be needed. In late October the UN General Assembly again voted for a resolution calling for an end to the US embargo.

latest.text: CBS's 60 Minutes reported US-Cuba negotiations stalled earlier this year. A Cuban deputy foreign minister says tougher US measures are hurting Cubans, and Washington says food and medicine are not restricted.
OFAC barred US banks from keeping some accounts for Cuban entrepreneurs and ended group people-to-people travel licenses.
Trump said the US and Cuba would make a deal and that he did not expect to need the military.
Al Jazeera reports the US sanctioned Cuba's state oil company CUPET. Rubio said sanctions would continue until government change, and Hegseth hinted at military options.
SCMP says the CUPET sanctions came hours after China-Cuba party talks, and Hegseth said at Guantanamo the Pentagon would be postured for any contingency.
Diaz-Canel warned a US attack would cause a bloodbath as Washington sanctioned Cuba's intelligence agency and ministers (AFP).

us_impact.text: The confrontation is mostly economic. US limits on travel and banking affect some Americans and Cuban-American families, and hardship on the island could raise migration. No US military action has been reported.

conflicts.watch: Any US naval blockade or military move around Cuba would raise both severity and US impact.
conflicts.outlook: Pressure is economic for now; a naval quarantine or a mass migration event would change that.
conflicts.consensus: AFP and Caribbean outlets agree on the sanctions; Cuba calls them economic warfare.

week_verdict.why: CBS reports stalled talks and continued pressure, with no new measures this week

cyber.title: Iran-linked intrusions into US water controllers
cyber.method: Intrusions into industrial controllers from Rockwell, Schneider Electric and Siemens.
cyber.summary: ABC reported in August that water-sector intrusions reached at least 12 states, with no widespread supply disruption. The IRGC-linked group CyberAv3ngers claimed the campaign, per CSIS. NBC reported unsuccessful attempts on US telecom and energy systems.
cyber.us_why: The intrusions happened in the US. The FBI, NSA, DOE and CISA warned that Iranian actors target these controllers, but the US government has not publicly attributed the campaign.
cyber.what_to_watch: Any new CISA advisory, or a water-supply disruption tied to these controllers.

sources.text: NBC News reported on Sept 2, citing four sources, that Iranian hackers also tried to reach US telecom and energy systems. The attempts were reported as unsuccessful so far.
CSIS's incident list says the IRGC-linked CyberAv3ngers claimed the August water campaign across at least a dozen states. It says the US government had not publicly attributed it.

ABC News reported on Aug 4, citing sources, that water-sector intrusions reached at least 12 states, with Iran the prime suspect. Involvement was unconfirmed and supplies saw no widespread disruption.

TechCrunch reports an updated advisory from the FBI, NSA, DOE and CISA. It says Iranian actors target controllers from Rockwell, Schneider Electric and Siemens. Those products are also used in the US.

cyber.title: Volt Typhoon's 'Silent Train' relay network
cyber.method: A covert relay network of hijacked routers used in four zero-day campaigns on edge systems.
cyber.summary: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs says the Chinese group Volt Typhoon used a relay network it calls Silent Train. Targets were mostly US government, defence and university networks. Sessions are short and tools are wiped afterward, which makes detection hard.
cyber.us_why: Lumen says US networks were the main targets, using TP-Link, Netgear and Fortinet devices sold in the US. The notes contain no new US government statement.
cyber.what_to_watch: A CISA or FBI advisory on Silent Train, or a takedown.

sources.text: BleepingComputer says Silent Train sessions are short, with tools wiped afterward, which makes detection hard. Lumen says it was partly a response to the FBI's earlier KV-botnet takedown.
Black Lotus Labs (Lumen) says Chinese group Volt Typhoon used a covert relay network, Silent Train, in four zero-day campaigns against management and edge systems.

Nextgov says Lumen found Silent Train targets mostly US government, defense and university networks, concentrated in Hawaii, California and Texas. It used TP-Link, Netgear and Fortinet devices also sold in the US.
